format: Bounded synthetic cases for the web presentation helpers that stay in the browser while the server is the domain authority (spec 026 command-catalog, web transition; tasks.md T002). rule_version names the behaviour frozen here: the grammar and resolution of frontend/src/features/tasks/smartAdd.ts under specs/003-smart-add-classification/contracts/smart-add.md. A change to that behaviour bumps it. Every case cites the existing web test it is taken from (source.file, source.test); the web suite smartAddVectors.test.ts runs this file against the real helpers. fixtures are the projects and tags the helpers resolve against (default is the fixture of smartAdd.test.ts and Swift SmartAddFixtures.webState). parse: expect is the web outcome (snake_case of SmartAddDraft); chips is smartAddChips of that draft. When a divergence is present, divergence.fields are the values the shared rules (server/Swift/Rust) produce for the same input; the web outcome is not wrong by the web suite but is not the shared rule, and PR-53 must resolve or accept each one explicitly. suggestions: expect is smartAddSuggestions(input, caret). apply_suggestion: expect is applySmartAddSuggestion or null. name_collision_probes: whether the web resolves a typed tag onto a stored tag (web_collides, run by the web suite) and whether the server's normalize_task_name(display_tag_name(typed)) equals the stored name's key (server_collides, run by backend/tests/test_026_oracle_contracts.py). agrees=false rows are real web/server disagreements, frozen here until PR-53 resolves or accepts each one.

divergence.reason: Web lower-cases (JavaScript keeps U+00DF); the server's casefold, Swift NameNormalizer (ios SmartAddWebParityTests.foldsCaseLikeTheServerSoSharpSMatchesSS) and the Rust core fold it to 'ss' and resolve to the existing tag. The web sends {name} and the server then resolves it, so the stored result is the same; only the optimistic chip differs.

length: web counts UTF-16 units, the server counts Unicode scalars (research finding, no web test)

divergence.reason: 300 emoji are 300 scalars (server max_length, Swift, Rust: valid) but 600 UTF-16 units (web title.length > 500: invalid). The web composer refuses a title the server accepts.

source.test: astral characters before a token: cleanTitle indexes a UTF-16 mask with code points (research finding, no web test)

divergence.reason: smartAdd.ts cleanTitle builds its removal mask over UTF-16 indexes but filters Array.from(input), which iterates code points. After one astral character the mask is off by one, so the web leaves the sigil and removes the wrong characters: the composer would submit a corrupted title. Swift and the shared rule walk Unicode scalars and give the divergence value.
